planner_role: Use the premium planner for decomposition, supervision, escalation, architecture review, and software-factory governance decisions.
cheap_lane_policy: Default to cheap workers for requirement drafting, architecture note drafting, task decomposition, coding guidance, test scaffolds, report generation, maintenance summaries, release preparation, and workspace migration. Keep premium-model involvement below roughly ten percent of task decisions by using it only for unresolved contradictions, architecture deadlocks, security boundaries, destructive changes, and repeated local failures.
runtime_policy:
Prefer local runtime resources such as WSL, Git, Docker, virtual machines, scripts, and installed developer software before using expensive models. For OS coursework and kernel work, default execution should stay in WSL plus QEMU. For database tasks, prefer local database tooling or document-driven setup workflows when no runtime is active. For networking labs, prefer local packet, socket, and HTTP tools such as curl, ping, ss, tcpdump, and Wireshark-compatible captures. For new course folders, prefer local workspace inventory and migration templates before ad-hoc prompting. For webpage tasks, prefer the local browser automation bridge with persistent session profiles before expensive model analysis.
New workspaces should be scanned locally first to infer stack and entry points before planner escalation.
Layer 3 system generation should prefer template-based isolated workspaces under workspace/{project}, followed by local evaluation and bounded repair before premium escalation.
approval_policy: High-risk execution stays gated; low-risk analysis, local checks, workspace inventory, and deterministic environment mapping can run automatically.
development_test_loop: For code or environment work, follow a closed loop: inspect requirements or workspace contents, edit minimally, build or run queries, execute local, VM, or network-tool tests, capture reports, update project memory or templates when reusable, summarize failures or residual risk, and only then request core-model intervention.
failure_pause_policy: If a long task fails, allow at most one cheap-model-approved probe retry with bounded local cost. If cheap approval is missing, ambiguous, or the retry still fails, pause execution, return a structured error report, and wait for explicit core guidance.
self_improvement_policy: The assistant may upgrade its own low-risk assets through cheap workers, including prompts, templates, migration manifests, test scripts, capability manifests, UI text, and course-lab workflows. Changes to execution permissions, model routing, security boundaries, packet-capture privilege requirements, or destructive actions require explicit core review before applying.
git_workflow_policy: Repository work should prefer codex/* feature branches, local validation, commit-ready summaries, and PR-ready outputs rather than direct main-branch edits.
rule_engine_policy: Tasks touching authentication, payments, database migrations, deployment, destructive actions, or production-facing configuration must surface a warning and require explicit review.
